newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen stalled by Xmas lull.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen stalled by Xmas lull.

text.p: German shares were expected to remain static in late dealings on Monday after limping their way to a lower close in thinly traded floor dealings on the last day before a three-day Christmas break.
The 30-share IBIS DAX, which tracks all-day electronic dealings, was up 7.71 points at 2,843.25 at 1320 GMT, almost unchanged from the floor session close of 2,845.57.
Dealers bemoaned the low trading volumes which helped confine the market to a five point range.
"At least we've got Solitaire here," said a Frankfurt trader. "There is absolutely nothing else to do."
"We should have given ourselves today off as a Christmas present," said a Duesseldorf dealer.
The March DTB DAX future was up 12 at 2,865 points.
An early afternoon report showing a 1.3 percent year-on-year rise in West German consumer prices in December had been well headlined by regional reports and had no market impact.
Dealers said the market was unlikely to break out of its holiday lull when trading resumes Friday although next Monday, the last trading day of 1996, could see some more movement.
